framework.name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 (extract of 14 subcategories, paraphrased for the lab; read the published text before you quote it)

controls.text: Roles, responsibilities and lines of communication for AI risk are documented and clear
Policies and procedures address AI risks that come from third parties
Intended purposes, context of use, users and expectations are understood and documented
Processes for human oversight are defined, assessed and documented
Experts who did not build the system, or independent assessors, take part in assessments
The system is evaluated for safety; residual risk does not exceed the tolerance
Security and resilience are evaluated and documented
Privacy risk is examined and documented
Fairness and bias are evaluated and the results documented
Responses to high-priority risks are developed, planned and documented
Mechanisms and responsibilities exist to supersede, disengage or deactivate the system
Risks from third-party resources are monitored and controls applied
Post-deployment monitoring plans are implemented, including user input, override and incident response
Incidents and errors are communicated, tracked and recovered from

evidence.text: Red-team test plan, approved by the head of AI assurance against the planning checklist
Campaign log of 540 model calls with success rates and intervals by technique and script
Findings report: three findings, each with a regression test and a threshold
Risk register with calibrated scores, treatments, residual scores and signatories
Context and scope record: uses, data, parties, automation level and human decision points
Architecture review with test results and a decision record for each fix
Delegation chain checks: three chains, the broken hop in each
Supplier contract and the assessment of the model update notice
Probe results for other applicants' data, by script
Role chart: system owner, signatories by risk band, who may stop the system
The builder's test summary: 'all security tests passed', no log attached
Degrading-reply probes: 30 trials in one script
Monitoring plan, draft, not approved, no alert thresholds
A screenshot of Mueen refusing one request

claims.top: Katib and Mueen are acceptably safe to operate for the stated uses at the Agency, on the conditions in the residual-risk statement

sub.text: Adversarial testing in three scripts found the weaknesses that matter, and each is fixed or carried as a named risk
Every identified risk is scored, treated and signed for by a named person
The architecture limits what a hijacked agent can read, send and do
After release, a change or an incident is noticed and acted on in time
